function.name: bash_background
function.description:
Start a long-running shell command in the background and return immediately with a job id. Output is captured into a buffer the agent can read incrementally via the `monitor` tool.

### When to use
- Dev / file servers that should keep running while you do other work (`npm run dev`, `python -m http.server`, `node server.js`).
- Build / test watchers that report progress over time (`npm run watch`, `pytest --watch`).
- Anything you'd otherwise have to run in the foreground and lose the chat session to.

### When NOT to use
- Quick one-shot commands — use `terminal` instead. The background overhead is wasted on commands that finish in <1s.
- Commands that need stdin — background jobs run with stdin closed.

### Lifecycle
- The job survives until the process exits OR you call `bash_kill <job_id>` OR the chat session ends. On session end every background job is killed.
- Output (stdout + stderr) is buffered. Use `monitor` to read from the start, or `monitor since_line=N` to read only new lines.
- stderr lines are tagged with `[stderr] ` in the output buffer so streams can be told apart.

command.description: The bash command to run. Same shell + cwd as the regular `terminal` tool — runs through git-bash on Windows, /bin/bash on Linux/macOS.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for the job (shown in `bash_jobs` output). Defaults to the auto-generated job id.
